How eutrophisation affect food web structures along the estuary-sea continuum

Summary

library(renv)
renv::load()
library(targets)
library(here)
tar_config_set(
  store = here::here("_targets")
)

library(ggplot2)
set_theme(theme_minimal())
library(dplyr)
library(riversea)

Estuary classification

First, we have different zones that we can download from the Sandre database. They take the form of polygons.

area <- tar_read(hydrographic_area)
head(area)

By investigating with mapview, we can see that there is a zone missing near Le Havre.

We can match food webs to zone either if they fit within a polygon, or if they are very close to it (e.g. less than 5km away).

To classify food webs in different bassin, we use the define of the hydrographic district given by the DCE. It is a very broad geographical unit, but we will start from there.

fw_with_district <- tar_read(fw_with_district)

library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthhires)
coastline <- ne_coastline(scale = "large", returnclass = "sf")

ggplot(fw_with_district, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, color = district)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_sf(data = coastline, inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_color_viridis_d() +
  coord_sf(
    xlim = range(fw_with_district$longitude),
    ylim = range(fw_with_district$latitude)
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, color = "Hydrographic district")

We will later this classification to model it as a random effect to take into account the differences that can be due to the hydrographic bassin.

First models

Format the data

# Food web with zone information (DCE hydrographic district).
district <- tar_read(fw_with_district) |>
  select(trait, district, zone_id)

# Food web with environment information.
environment <- tar_read(fw_with_env) |>
  filter(dist_to_env < 5) |>
  select(-foodweb) |>
  mutate(
    salinity = scale(log10(sali_mean)) |> as.numeric(),
    chlorophyll = scale(chl_mean) |> as.numeric()
  )

size <- tar_read(foodweb_size_info)

data <- inner_join(district, environment, by = join_by(trait)) |>
  mutate(log_trophic_richness = scale(log_trophic_richness) |> as.numeric()) |>
  left_join(size, by = join_by(trait)) |>
  mutate(max_fish_size = tidyr::replace_na(max_fish_size, 0))

SEM

data <- data |>
  select(
    log_species_richness,
    log_trophic_richness,
    salinity,
    chlorophyll,
    temp_mean,
    frac_piscivorous,
    connectance,
    trophic_length,
    year,
    zone_id,
    survey,
    max_fish_size
  ) |>
  filter_out(is.na(zone_id)) |>
  mutate(zone_id = as.factor(zone_id)) |>
  mutate(max_fish_size = max_fish_size |> scale() |> as.numeric())

observable <- c("salinity", "chlorophyll", "temp_mean")
mediator <- c("log_species_richness", "max_fish_size", "frac_piscivorous")
response <- c("trophic_length", "connectance")
random <- c("(1 | year)", "(1 | zone_id)")
sem_model <- build_sem(observable, mediator, response, random, data)
piecewiseSEM::coefs(sem_model)

Fit the models

We fit three models to begin with that consider trophic length is shaped by 1. salinity and chlorophyll 2. salinity, chlorophyll and their interactions 3. salinity, chlorophyll and trophic richness (number of nodes in the local web)

library(INLA)

data <- data |>
  mutate(
    connectance = connectance |> scale() |> as.numeric(),
    trophic_length = trophic_length |> scale() |> as.numeric(),
  )

m_c <- inla(
  connectance ~ 1 + salinity * chlorophyll +
    f(year, model = "iid") + f(survey, model = "iid") +
    f(zone_id, model = "iid"),
  data = data
)

m_tl <- inla(
  trophic_length ~ 1 + salinity * chlorophyll +
    f(year, model = "iid") + f(survey, model = "iid") +
    f(zone_id, model = "iid"),
  data = data
)

Visualise fixed effects

extract_fixed <- function(model, model_name) {
  model$summary.fixed |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column("term") |>
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
    mutate(model = model_name)
}

fixed <- bind_rows(
  extract_fixed(m_c, "Connectance"),
  extract_fixed(m_tl, "Trophic length")
)

ggplot(fixed, aes(x = mean, y = term, color = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = `0.025quant`, xmax = `0.975quant`),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(x = `0.5quant`),
    size = 3,
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)
  ) +
  labs(x = "Effect size", y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

We see that the main driver of trophic length is clearly trophic richness. The effects of salinity and chlorophyll in the two models that do not include richness appear to be a consequence of their correlation of with richness and not a direct effect.

It is partly expected. Trophic structure can be shaped by three factors: trophic richness, individual sizes, and their predation window. As we have for now taken the same predation window for all species, only effect of environmental drivers on indivdual sizes could explain variation in trophic structure. Probably by refining predation window and species diet we will be able to capture an effect of environmental driver beyond pure richness effects.

If we further compare these two models, we see that the interaction between salinity and chlorophyll overlaps with zero, indicating that it does not influence community trophic length.

Visualise marginal effets

salinity_vals <- seq(min(data$salinity), max(data$salinity), length.out = 100)

prediction_salinity <- data.frame(
  salinity    = salinity_vals,
  chlorophyll = 0, # held at mean (scaled)
  year        = NA,
  survey      = NA,
  district    = NA
)

data_pred <- bind_rows(data, prediction_salinity)
m_pred_salinity <- inla(
  connectance ~ 1 + salinity * chlorophyll +
    f(year, model = "iid") + f(survey, model = "iid") +
    f(zone_id, model = "iid"),
  data = data_pred,
  control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, link = 1)
)

# extract predictions for the NA rows
n_obs <- nrow(data)
preds <- m_pred_salinity$summary.fitted.values[(n_obs + 1):(n_obs + 100), ]

prediction_salinity |>
  bind_cols(preds) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = salinity_vals)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = `0.025quant`, ymax = `0.975quant`), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = mean)) +
  geom_point(data = data, aes(x = salinity, y = trophic_length), alpha = 0.1) +
  labs(x = "Salinity (scaled)", y = "Trophic length")
chlorophyll_vals <- seq(
  min(data$chlorophyll), max(data$chlorophyll),
  length.out = 100
)

prediction_chlorophyll <- data.frame(
  chlorophyll = chlorophyll_vals,
  salinity = 0, # held at mean (scaled)
  year = NA,
  survey = NA,
  district = NA
)

data_pred <- bind_rows(data, prediction_chlorophyll)
m_pred_chlorophyll <- inla(
  connectance ~ 1 + salinity * chlorophyll +
    f(year, model = "iid") + f(survey, model = "iid") +
    f(zone_id, model = "iid"),
  data = data_pred,
  control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE, link = 1)
)

# extract predictions for the NA rows
n_obs <- nrow(data)
preds <- m_pred_chlorophyll$summary.fitted.values[(n_obs + 1):(n_obs + 100), ]

prediction_chlorophyll |>
  bind_cols(preds) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = chlorophyll_vals)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = `0.025quant`, ymax = `0.975quant`), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = mean)) +
  geom_point(data = data, aes(x = chlorophyll, y = trophic_length), alpha = 0.1) +
  labs(x = "Chlorophyll (scaled)", y = "Trophic length")

Visualise random effects

Temporal

year_re <- m_c$summary.random$year |>
  as_tibble() |>
  rename(year = ID)

ggplot(year_re, aes(x = year, y = mean)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = `0.025quant`, ymax = `0.975quant`), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Year random effect on trophic length") +
  theme_minimal()

Spatial

area <- tar_read(hydrographic_area)
spatial_re <- m_c$summary.random$zone_id |>
  as_tibble() |>
  rename(zone_id = ID) |>
  left_join(area, by = join_by(zone_id)) |>
  st_as_sf()

bbox <- st_bbox(spatial_re)

ggplot(spatial_re) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = mean)) +
  geom_sf(data = coastline) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "steelblue", mid = "white", high = "tomato",
    midpoint = 0, name = "RE"
  ) +
  coord_sf(
    xlim = c(bbox["xmin"], bbox["xmax"]),
    ylim = c(bbox["ymin"], bbox["ymax"])
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
